item.title: Corte de apelaciones de EEUU confirma la inclusión de Anthropic en lista negra del Pentágono
item.description: Una corte federal de apelaciones declinó bloquear el viernes una orden del Departamento de Defensa que incluía a Anthropic en una lista negra de contratos militares y consideraba a esta compañía de inteligencia artificial un riesgo para la seguridad nacional.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Una corte federal de apelaciones declinó bloquear el viernes una orden del Departamento de Defensa que incluía a Anthropic en una lista negra de contratos militares y consideraba a esta compañía de inteligencia artificial un riesgo para la seguridad nacional. La sentencia de la Corte de Apelaciones para el Circuito del Distrito de Columbia se dictó en el marco de una demanda interpuesta por Anthropic contra la decisión del Pentágono de calificarla como un riesgo para la cadena de suministro en materia de seguridad nacional. La empresa indicó que esta decisión ha supuesto pérdidas por valor de miles de millones de dólares y ha dañado su reputación de cara a su esperada próxima salida a bolsa. Anthropic declaró en un comunicado que, aunque discrepa respetuosamente de la decisión, sigue confiando en su postura y está barajando sus opciones, incluida una nueva revisión judicial. El mes pasado, un juez federal de San Francisco anuló una designación paralela en virtud de otra ley, al considerar que el Gobierno había tomado represalias ilegales contra Anthropic por sus opiniones sobre la seguridad de la IA.

item.title: George Russell grabs 5th pole of season at Azerbaijan
item.description: Mercedes' George Russell clinched his fifth Formula 1 pole of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mercedes' George Russell clinched his fifth Formula 1 pole of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on Friday. The Brit roared through the Baku street circuit in a time of 1:42.526 in Q3, comfortably ahead of runner-up Charles Leclerc of Ferrari at 1:43.363. McLaren's Oscar Piastri was third, just 0.001 seconds behind Leclerc. Russell will be looking for his third win of the season on Saturday after finishing second to Red Bull's Max Verstappen at last year's Azerbaijan GP. Mercedes teammate and current F1 points leader Kimi Antonelli of Italy crashed out of Q1 and will start 16th. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar returned from a wrist injury and qualified fourth in his first action since the Hungarian GP on July 26. The remainder of the top 10, in order, are McLaren's Lando Norris, Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, Alpine's Pierre Gasly, Verstappen, Williams' Carlos Sainz and Alpine's Franco Colapinto. --Field Level Media

item.title: Knicks' Jalen Brunson 'fully cleared' after wrist surgery
item.description: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson said he is "fully cleared" to return following offseason wrist surgery.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson said he is "fully cleared" to return following offseason wrist surgery. The All-Star point guard had a procedure on his left wrist in July after leading New York to its first title in 53 years. Brunson, 30, confirmed his readiness during an appearance Thursday on his "Roommates Show" on YouTube. "As you guys know, I had surgery this offseason, and I just wanted to tell you guys that I am fully cleared," he told the crowd during a live taping at Randall's Island Park in New York City. The 2026 Finals MVP averaged a playoff-high 28.4 points in the Knicks' 16-3 playoff march to the championship. Brunson averaged 26.0 points, 6.8 assists and 3.3 rebounds in 74 games (all starts) during the 2025-26 regular season. The Knicks' preseason opener is Oct. 5 at Philadelphia. They open the regular season at home against the 76ers on Oct. 20. --Field Level Media

item.title: Perplexity AI sued by startup for allegedly stealing 'wake word' technology
item.description: Startup DaVoice has sued Perplexity AI in California federal court for allegedly stealing trade secrets related to "wake word" technology for AI assistants.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: Startup DaVoice has sued Perplexity AI in California federal court for allegedly stealing trade secrets related to "wake word" technology for AI assistants. The heavily redacted complaint , filed on Thursday, said that Perplexity stole DaVoice's secrets after the companies collaborated on unspecified technology "built with DaVoice’s proprietary source code, inference logic, network architecture, training approaches, training data, and know-how." Spokespeople for the companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Friday. DaVoice specializes in technology that allows devices to continuously listen for "wake words" to activate them. The startup said that it has collaborated with companies including Volkswagen and internet-of-things company Samsara. Perplexity is best known for its AI-powered search engine technology and Comet browser and AI assistant The case is DaVoice v. Perplexity AI Inc, US District Court for the Northern District of California, No. 3:26-cv-10909. For DaVoice: Davida Brook and Ian Crosby of Susman Godfrey For Perplexity: attorney information not yet available

item.title: Iran will make no nuclear concessions, Iranian official says
item.description: Iran will show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the United States accepts its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which calls for steps including the lifting of a US naval blockade on Iranian ports, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran will show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the United States accepts its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which calls for steps including the lifting of a US naval blockade on Iranian ports, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday. The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the waterway would remain closed until “all of Iran’s conditions are met” by the United States. Under [USN:L6N45H06Z TEXT:"Iran’s proposal"], Tehran has offered to reopen the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. Within seven days, hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon, the United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen funds and waive its oil sanctions, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Thursday. The proposal follows a sharp escalation in Middle East tensions after seven months of war between Iran and the United States, with Iran-backed Houthi militias in Yemen launching missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Congo military plane crash kills 13, including three officers, official says
item.description: Thirteen people including three army officers were killed on Friday when a military plane crashed in Democratic Republic of Congo, an official said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thirteen people including three army officers were killed on Friday when a military plane crashed in Democratic Republic of Congo, an official said. The plane was travelling to the capital, Kinshasa, from the southwestern city of Kikwit when it experienced a technical problem and attempted to land in Kenge, in Kwango province, said Remy Saki Bokinda, the Kwango vice governor. "With no landing strip available in Kenge, the plane crashed into a residential plot," he said. The passengers included General Likulia Bakumi, the army's auditor general, as well as a major, a captain and other military personnel and civilians, Bokinda said. "All those on board died; 12 were burned beyond recognition, while the pilot's lifeless body was found outside the aircraft," he said. Congo's aviation accident investigation authority is launching a probe of the crash, a government statement said. Congo's army suffered significant setbacks last year at the hands of Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 rebels who seized large swathes of the east.

item.title: Argentina pode obter uma receita agrícola quase recorde em 2027, prevê bolsa
item.description: A Argentina poderia obter uma receita quase recorde com as exportações agrícolas no próximo ano, já que os preços elevados das safras, uma colheita excepcional e interrupções no abastecimento em regiões exportadoras concorrentes impulsionam os embarques de grãos e o influxo de moeda forte, informou a Bolsa de Comércio de Rosário em um relatório divulgado na sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Kylie Madry
item.content:encoded: A Argentina poderia obter uma receita quase recorde com as exportações agrícolas no próximo ano, já que os preços elevados das safras, uma colheita excepcional e interrupções no abastecimento em regiões exportadoras concorrentes impulsionam os embarques de grãos e o influxo de moeda forte, informou a Bolsa de Comércio de Rosário em um relatório divulgado na sexta-feira. O setor agrícola poderia gerar cerca de US$40 bilhões em receitas de exportação em 2027, o que seria o segundo maior total anual já registrado, ficando atrás apenas de 2022, de acordo com o relatório. Para 2026, a bolsa estima US$35,2 bilhões. As exportações agrícolas são a principal fonte de moeda estrangeira da Argentina, fundamental para reabastecer as reservas do banco central, estabilizar o peso e sustentar as finanças públicas. A bolsa projeta que a safra total de grãos da Argentina em 2026/27 será de 156 milhões de toneladas métricas, uma das maiores já registradas. Os preços internacionais do milho, do trigo e da soja têm sido sustentados por riscos de abastecimento relacionados ao conflito no Mar Negro, onde a interrupção das exportações russas e ucranianas reduziu a disponibilidade, segundo o relatório. Os agricultores argentinos se beneficiaram dessa interrupção, afirmou a bolsa em um relatório separado, com vendas de milho acima de 1 milhão de toneladas por semana durante quatro semanas consecutivas e os compromissos de exportação de trigo atingindo seu nível mais alto em cinco anos para esta época da safra. A demanda da Ásia tem sido notável, com compradores como a Indonésia se voltando para as safras argentinas. A bolsa também informou que a arrecadação com impostos de exportação de grãos e subprodutos poderia subir para US$5,48 bilhões em 2027, um aumento de 16% em relação a este ano, mesmo que as alíquotas tributárias devam diminuir.

item.title: Mpox case confirmed in northeastern Congolese city at center of Ebola outbreak
item.description: A laboratory-confirmed case of mpox was identified in the northeastern Congolese city of Bunia, the director of a local hospital and two health officials said, raising concerns about a resurgence of the disease as the country battles its worst Ebola outbreak on record.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A laboratory-confirmed case of mpox was identified in the northeastern Congolese city of Bunia, the director of a local hospital and two health officials said, raising concerns about a resurgence of the disease as the country battles its worst Ebola outbreak on record. The epidemic caused by the [USN:L6N45H0P8 TEXT:"Ebola outbreak"] was declared on May 15 in Ituri province, where Bunia is located, and has infected 7,890 people and killed 3,799, according to government data published on Thursday. Mpox is a viral disease that causes fever and skin lesions and spreads through close physical contact. Congo declared an end to mpox as a national public health emergency in April after a three-year outbreak that resulted in more than 34,000 confirmed cases nationwide. Authorities cautioned at the time that the virus had not been eradicated and could resurge. The latest case involves a 21-year-old woman who was admitted to hospital on Thursday with lesions across her body consistent with mpox, hospital director Davin Ambitapio Musungufu said. She tested positive on Friday, he and two health officials told Reuters. A second woman, aged 32, has been identified as a suspected mpox case and is awaiting laboratory results, Musungufu said. She and the confirmed patient have been isolated and are being cared for by a dedicated medical team. Investigations are underway to trace contacts and identify the source of infection, Musungufu said. Dr. Adelard Lofungola, a health official who served as deputy incident manager for Congo's mpox response, said five suspected mpox cases in Bunia were currently under investigation. Health officials have reported an increase in mpox cases in several parts of the country over the past month, he said. Lofungola said the Ebola outbreak's impact on Congo's health system was complicating efforts to monitor other infections.

item.title: UK's Pinewood Technologies shareholders approve $721 million Ridgeview takeover
item.description: Shareholders of British automotive software firm Pinewood Technologies on Friday approved a £545 million ($721.14 million) take-private deal by US private equity firm Ridgeview Partners.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shareholders of British automotive software firm Pinewood Technologies (PINE.L) on Friday approved a £545 million ($721.14 million) take-private deal by US private equity firm Ridgeview Partners. At a shareholder meeting on Friday, 99.76% of votes cast were in support of the takeover. Pinewood's board in August [USN:L4N44G0MH TEXT:"had recommended"] Ridgeview’s offer valuing the company at £4.48 per share in cash. Pinewood is the latest London-listed technology company to attract private equity interest as buyout firms continue to target UK-listed businesses seen as [USN:L6N42Y0HI TEXT:"undervalued"]. The deal is expected to become effective on October 9. Pinewood provides a cloud-based platform to help car dealerships and manufacturers manage everything from vehicle sales and customer relationships to repairs and accounting. Pinewood had also attracted interest from Apax Partners [USN:L4N3Z91Q8 TEXT:"in"][USN:L4N3Z91Q8 TEXT:" January"], with an offer valuing it at 500 pence-per-share. But the private equity firm [USN:L4N3Z91QU TEXT:"withdrew"] its approach in February citing challenging market conditions. Shares of Pinewood have gained about 24.16% year-to-date. ($1 = 0.7557 pounds)

item.title: US refiner Phillips 66 is using AI to predict outages and boost processing, executive says
item.description: Phillips 66 is using artificial intelligence to predict outages within its refining systems, save on maintenance costs and increase crude processing, said Tandra Perkins, an executive vice president at the US refiner.
item.dc:creator: Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: Phillips 66 (PSX.N) is using artificial intelligence to predict outages within its refining systems, save on maintenance costs and increase crude processing, said Tandra Perkins, an executive vice president at the US refiner. "I need my systems up more than they're down, being able to predict that obviously saves on maintenance costs," Perkins said on Friday while speaking at the Reuters Momentum AI conference in Austin, Texas. The increased availability allows for more crude to be processed by the refiner and capture more margins, Perkins said, without providing a number on cost savings. The Houston-headquartered company, which has about 10 refineries, has been focused on operational cost savings, particularly on the refining side.

item.title: India's Zee escalates copyright fight against Reliance-Disney's JioStar
item.description: India's Zee Entertainment has asked the Delhi High Court to initiate contempt proceedings against Reliance-Disney joint venture JioStar, alleging it continued to use copyrighted content despite a court injunction, a legal filing shows.
item.dc:creator: Arpan Chaturvedi
item.content:encoded: India's Zee Entertainment has asked the Delhi High Court to initiate contempt proceedings against Reliance-Disney joint venture JioStar, alleging it continued to use copyrighted content [USN:L4N41J12I TEXT:"despite a court injunction"], a legal filing shows. The filing, dated September 21, escalates an ongoing copyright dispute between the companies. Zee alleges JioStar is guilty of "wilful disobedience" because it continued using Zee's music and songs in programmes broadcast on its platforms despite a court order barring such use. JioStar, formed from the $8.5 billion merger of Reliance and Disney's Indian media assets in 2024, declined to comment. Zee did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The copyright case was heard on Friday. A source aware of the details of Friday's court hearing told Reuters the Delhi High Court asked JioStar for a response to Zee's latest allegations and the case will be heard next in December. The lawsuit began in April when Zee sought $3 million in damages, citing 50 alleged copyright violations involving content from its music division. In May, the Delhi High Court ordered JioStar not to "use, publish, broadcast, stream, upload" any of Zee's licensed works. JioStar's lawyers have previously told the court the alleged infringements were "unintentional" and "purely residual in nature". The company said in May that it had removed a substantial volume of Zee content following the expiry of licensing agreements. In its latest filing, Zee cited six instances between May and July that it said showed the continued use of its copyrighted works by JioStar. JioStar is "illegally and actively exploiting" the works, Zee said in the filing. The case is one of several copyright disputes highlighting increasing competition over content rights as India's streaming and broadcasting market consolidates. JioStar, backed by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, is India's largest media and entertainment company. Zee, one of India's oldest broadcasters, is a smaller rival. The Disney-Reliance joint venture has also previously [USN:L4N41R1DU TEXT:"launched"] a legal battle against Zee, alleging the unauthorised broadcast of popular Bollywood movies at a time when JioStar held the rights to the content.

item.title: Report: 49ers DE Nick Bosa (calf) out multiple weeks
item.description: San Francisco 49ers pass rusher Nick Bosa will be sidelined for a "few weeks" with a calf injury, ESPN reported on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: San Francisco 49ers pass rusher Nick Bosa will be sidelined for a "few weeks" with a calf injury, ESPN reported on Friday. The five-time Pro Bowler sustained the injury during practice Thursday and could land on injured reserve, per the report. Bosa is not expected to play on Sunday when the 49ers (2-0) host the Arizona Cardinals (1-1) in Santa Clara, Calif. Bosa, 28, played a total of 70 snaps in the first two games while coming back from a torn right ACL sustained in Week 3 last season. He has recorded seven tackles (two for loss) with one quarterback hit. Bosa has recorded 64.5 sacks, 13 forced fumbles, 169 QB hits and 285 tackles in 87 games (85 starts) since being drafted with the No. 2 overall pick by San Francisco in 2019. --Field Level Media

item.title: Syracuse gains commitment of 5-star F Moussa Kamissoko
item.description: New Syracuse coach Gerry McNamara received a commitment Friday from Class of 2027 forward Moussa Kamissoko, just the second five-star recruit for the Orange in the past decade.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Syracuse coach Gerry McNamara received a commitment Friday from Class of 2027 forward Moussa Kamissoko, just the second five-star recruit for the Orange in the past decade. The 6-foot-7, 180-pound Kamissoko attends SPIRE Academy in Geneva, Ohio. The 247Sports composite lists him as the No. 5 small forward and the No. 14 overall player in the nation in the class. He played last season at Long Island Lutheran. The competition had been fierce for Kamissoko. He already took official visits to Illinois, BYU, Florida State, Virginia and Oklahoma State. Programs such as Alabama, NC State, Penn State and Providence also were trying to get his commitment. A scheduled visit to UConn on Friday presumably was canceled. He also had visits to Baylor and Louisville arranged for next month. Kamissoko is the first five-star prospect to pick the Orange since forward Donnie Freeman in 2024, per ESPN. He is the second player to commit to Syracuse in the 2027 recruiting cycle, joining Jack Donohue, a 6-8 forward from The Newman School in Boston. McNamara led Siena to a near-upset of No. 1 overall seed Duke in the first round of the NCAA Tournament last March. His name began swirling immediately when Syracuse fired Adrian Autry at the end of the season. Between his Siena success and his status as a program icon -- McNamara shared the court with fellow freshman Carmelo Anthony on the 2022-23 NCAA championship team -- he became the choice for the Orange. McNamara is being tasked with returning Syracuse basketball to national prominence. A team that seemed to be a virtual lock for the tournament each season hasn't been there since 2021. Syracuse finished last season with a 15-17 record (6-12 Atlantic Coast Conference). --Field Level Media
