Comercializadoras com presença relevante no segmento, como Matrix e Echoenergia, estão procurando focar na manutenção de sua carteira de clientes neste ano, em vez de expandi-la, enquanto se preparam para as próximas ondas de abertura de mercado. "O custo de aquisição do cliente é relativamente alto e agora o desconto que você consegue dar para esse cliente é pequeno. Então, diminuiu a atividade e diminuiu também a intensidade com a qual a gente atende a esse mercado", disse à Reuters Liu Aquino, CEO da geradora renovável e comercializadora Echoenergia, do grupo Equatorial (EQTL3.SA) . A Matrix, que detém a terceira maior carteira entre as comercializadoras varejistas do país, "estabilizou suas operações", diante do cenário desafiador de preços e de uma inadimplência mais elevada, afirmou Alexandre Gomes, vice-presidente comercial. Mas a companhia mantém a comercialização varejista como uma prioridade, enquanto se reestrutura e se desfaz de outros negócios, como ativos de geração distribuída solar, disse ele. "De fato, é a manutenção (da carteira), é levando uma experiência cada vez melhor para esse nosso cliente... que a gente entende que consegue replicar e ganhar escala, obviamente, dependendo das condições econômicas de abertura de mercado." Para Gomes, o preço não será o único recurso das comercializadoras para ganhar novos clientes. A Matrix, por exemplo, tem ofertado soluções agregadas, como baterias, a clientes como supermercados, que conseguem melhorar suas operações a partir da instalação desses equipamentos, apontou. O segmento varejista do setor elétrico abrange hoje cerca de 50 mil unidades consumidoras, respondendo por um volume de energia ainda pequeno diante de todo o mercado livre, que abriga também os grandes consumidores industriais. Mas esse quadro deve mudar a partir de novembro de 2027, com a autorização dada pelo governo brasileiro para migração de mais um grupo de estabelecimentos ligados em baixa tensão, como hospitais, escolas e outros, somando cerca de 6 milhões de consumidores. Já a partir de novembro de 2028, todos os 90 milhões de consumidores do país, incluindo residências, poderão escolher livremente seu fornecedor de energia. A mudança para o mercado livre não é obrigatória, de modo que o consumidor poderá continuar comprando energia de sua distribuidora local. Agentes do setor elétrico têm evitado fazer projeções sobre a velocidade das migrações a partir de 2027, apontando um elevado grau de incerteza.

item.title: Russia's Perm oil refinery halted operations after Friday drone attack, sources say
item.description: The Perm oil refinery, Russia's seventh-largest oil processing plant by volume, stopped operations following a Ukrainian drone attack, which caused a fire and damaged pipelines, storage and technological units on Friday, two industry sources said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Perm oil refinery, Russia's seventh-largest oil processing plant by volume, stopped operations following a Ukrainian drone attack, which caused a fire and damaged pipelines, storage and technological units on Friday, two industry sources said. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday he had discussed with US President Donald Trump efforts to end the four-year-old war with Russia, including a potential bilateral ceasefire on energy-related targets. Governor of Perm region, Dmitry Makhonin, said on his Telegram channel that an industrial site had came under attack on Friday, but did not name the plant. Lukoil, the refinery's owner, did not reply to a request for comment. The refinery was previously attacked on August 21. The plant, located 1,460 km (907 miles) northeast of Moscow, processed some 12.6 million tons, or 252,000 barrels per day, of oil in 2024. It produced 2 million tons of gasoline, 5.3 million tons of diesel, 200,000 tons of fuel oil and 700,000 tons of petroleum coke.

item.title: Votação da União Europeia sobre sistema de direção FSD da Tesla é adiada
item.description: A votação pela União Europeia sobre a autorização do sistema Full Self-Driving (FSD) supervisionado da Tesla em todo o bloco, prevista para outubro, foi adiada, e a próxima oportunidade para uma decisão não ocorrerá antes de dezembro, de acordo com uma agenda publicada no site da UE.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A votação pela União Europeia sobre a autorização do sistema Full Self-Driving (FSD) supervisionado da Tesla em todo o bloco, prevista para outubro, foi adiada, e a próxima oportunidade para uma decisão não ocorrerá antes de dezembro, de acordo com uma agenda publicada no site da UE. O órgão regulador holandês RDW aprovou o sistema em abril, com a Bélgica e alguns outros países seguindo o exemplo. O RDW também está propondo que o software de direção autônoma seja aprovado em todo o bloco. Já a Tesla informou em 1º de setembro, em uma postagem no X, que uma votação em toda a UE poderia ocorrer em 6 de outubro. No entanto, a pauta da reunião de 6 de outubro do Comitê Técnico de Veículos Motorizados (TCMV, na sigla em inglês), que reúne representantes dos Estados-membros da UE e da Comissão Europeia, lista apenas uma “continuação das discussões” sobre o pedido holandês de autorização nos termos do Artigo 39, com 25 minutos alocados para a discussão. O comitê já discutiu o pedido da Tesla em duas reuniões anteriores. A próxima reunião agendada do TCMV após outubro é em dezembro, o que torna essa a primeira oportunidade para uma votação com base na agenda atual. A implantação em toda a UE requer o apoio de uma “maioria qualificada” de 15 dos 27 Estados-membros do bloco, representando 65% da população. Vários países da UE, incluindo a Suécia, expressaram preocupações quanto ao FSD exceder os limites de velocidade, enquanto os países que o aprovaram afirmam que os motoristas continuam responsáveis pelo cumprimento das leis de trânsito. O mesmo comitê aprovou o sistema de assistência ao motorista BlueCruise da Ford (F.N) em março de 2024, tendo a Alemanha como patrocinadora. A Tesla considera a aprovação do FSD fundamental para impulsionar as vendas na Europa, onde busca recuperar participação de mercado em meio à crescente concorrência dos fabricantes chineses de veículos elétricos.

item.title: US appeals court upholds Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic
item.description: A federal appeals court on Friday declined to block a Defense Department order blacklisting Anthropic from military contracts and deeming the AI startup a national security risk.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A federal appeals court on Friday declined to block a Defense Department order [USN:L6N3ZT1EV TEXT:"blacklisting Anthropic"] from military contracts and deeming the AI startup a national security risk. The ruling from the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit came in a lawsuit by Anthropic challenging its designation by the Pentagon as a national security supply chain risk, which the startup says has cost it billions of dollars in lost business and damaged its reputation ahead of a [USN:L4N4291D9 TEXT:"highly anticipated initial public offering"]. Anthropic said in a statement that it respectfully disagrees with the decision but remains confident in its position and is considering its options, including further judicial review. A federal judge in San Francisco last month [USN:L6N40C0YN TEXT:"struck down a parallel designation"] under a different law, finding the administration had unlawfully retaliated against Anthropic for its views on AI safety.

item.title: Eli Lilly owes Nektar $90 mln in drug collaboration dispute, US jury says
item.description: A federal jury in California has determined that Eli Lilly must pay Nektar Therapeutics $90 million for breaking an agreement related to an autoimmune drug candidate that the companies developed together, according to a Nektar filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: A federal jury in California has determined that Eli Lilly (LLY.N) must pay Nektar Therapeutics (NKTR.O) $90 million for breaking an agreement related to an autoimmune drug candidate that the companies developed together, according to a Nektar filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The jury on Thursday agreed with Nektar that Lilly breached its duty of good faith by undermining the prospects for Rezpeg, developed to treat eczema, psoriasis and other conditions, after buying competitor Dermira. A Lilly spokesperson said in a statement on Friday that the jury "confirmed that Lilly used commercially reasonable efforts to develop Rezpeg as required by the contract and awarded only a small fraction of the damages Nektar sought." Nektar had requested $1 billion in damages, according to court filings. "We are very pleased with the jury’s verdict, finding that Eli Lilly, the largest pharmaceutical company in the world, breached its obligation to act in good faith," Nektar's lead attorney Diane Doolittle of Quinn Emanuel said in a statement. Nektar [USN:L1N39O17M TEXT:"said in the complaint"], filed in 2023, that Lilly purposely "botched" its analysis of their drug trials to make Rezpeg appear less effective and give it a pretext to terminate their agreement Lilly denied the allegations and said in a court filing that Rezpeg "did not yield acceptable clinical trial results according to the standards that Nektar and Lilly jointly developed and agreed to." The case is Nektar Therapeutics v. Eli Lilly & Co, US District Court for the Northern District of California, No. 3:23-cv-03943. For Nektar: Diane Doolittle of Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan For Lilly: Ryan Moorman of Kirkland & Ellis Read more: [USN:L1N39O17M TEXT:"Nektar Therapeutics sues Eli Lilly over autoimmune disease treatment"]

item.title: China y EEUU se interesan por proyectos mineros en Perú mientras gobierno urge elevar producción
item.description: Perú espera elevar su producción anual de cobre en un millón de toneladas en cinco a seis años con nuevos proyectos, mientras empresas chinas y estadounidenses evalúan inversiones en medio de una mayor competencia por minerales críticos en Sudamérica, dijo a Reuters el ministro de Energía y Minas, Guillermo Shinno.
item.dc:creator: Marco Aquino
item.content:encoded: Perú espera elevar su producción anual de cobre en un millón de toneladas en cinco a seis años con nuevos proyectos, mientras empresas chinas y estadounidenses evalúan inversiones en medio de una mayor competencia por minerales críticos en Sudamérica, dijo a Reuters el ministro de Energía y Minas, Guillermo Shinno. El país andino, el tercer mayor productor mundial de cobre, espera que su producción se mantenga este año en entre 2,5 y 2,7 millones de toneladas, prácticamente sin cambios desde el 2023 por la disminución de la ley del mineral, y en medio de recurrentes conflictos sociales, dijo el titular de la cartera. Shinno señaló que el gobierno de la presidenta Keiko Fujimori, que asumio a fines de julio, busca revertir este estancamiento simplificando los trámites burocráticos. En los últimos dos meses una veintena de empresas mineras han mostrado interés en desempolvar proyectos, dijo. Entre ellas de China, que compra el 73% del cobre que produce Perú; y de Estados Unidos, en momentos en que Washington busca expandir su presencia en las cadenas de suministro de minerales críticos. "Las expectativas son enormes, todos han estado preguntando y viniendo al ministerio para ver cómo pueden implementar sus proyectos", afirmó Shinno en una entrevista la noche del jueves. El ministro dijo que el Gobierno está comprometido en reducir el centenar de trámites en el sector, para atraer inversión. "Se ha identificado que podríamos eliminar 27 permisos", dijo Shinno. "No se trata de relajar el estándar ambiental, sino ser rigurosos y muy claros". Alrededor del 70% de los 64.000 millones de dólares de la cartera de proyectos mineros está vinculado al cobre, agregó. El ministro señaló que casi toda la inversión comprometida para este año, que sumarían unos 7.000 millones de dólares, son solo para fortalecer operaciones o para extender la vida de las minas. "Con nuevos proyectos previstos, en 5 o 6 años podríamos agregar un millón de toneladas de cobre mas por año", dijo. La minería es clave para la economía local porque sus ventas representan el 70% de las exportaciones totales del país. POTENCIALES PLANES Entre las firmas que se han acercado al despacho de Shinno, según registros del ministerio, figuran las chinas Las Bambas de MMG, Chinalco, Shougang y Jinzhao; las estadounidenses Newmont (NEM.N) y Freeport-McMoRan (FCX.N) , además de las globales First Quantum (FM.TO) , Barrick (ABX.TO) , Anglo American (AAL.L) y Glencore (GLEN.L) . El ministro dijo que First Quantum quiere avanzar con su proyecto de cobre La Granja, mientras que Chinalco adquirió en julio el proyecto Los Calatos, en el sur del país, y actualmente está realizando estudios ambientales previos a su desarrollo. First Quantum informó en un comunicado en mayo que actualizó los recursos en La Granja y describió al proyecto "como el segundo mayor recurso de cobre virgen del mundo". El Gobierno estima inversiones de 2.400 millones de dólares en La Granja y 655 millones de dólares en Los Calatos en los próximos años. Chinalco, que opera la mina Toromocho, y Las Bambas están entre las seis minas de cobre más grandes del Perú. Shinno afirmó que prevé asimismo una mayor inversión minera estadounidense mientras Washington busca reducir la influencia china en los minerales estratégicos. Estados Unidos y Perú firmaron en febrero un acuerdo de cooperación en minerales críticos, que el secretario de Estado estadounidense, Marco Rubio, destacó durante su visita a Lima en septiembre como una forma de aprovechar las nuevas oportunidades en el sector. "Todos aquellos que quieren invertir responsablemente y respetar las leyes peruanas son bienvenidos. No hay un trato discriminatorio. Esperemos que con esta nueva política que tiene Estados Unidos más empresas americanas se animen a venir", dijo Shinno. La estadounidense Freeport-McMoRan planea extender hasta el 2053 la vida de su mina de cobre en Perú, con una inversión de 2.100 millones de dólares, según el ministerio peruano.

item.title: Chinese, US firms line up for Peru copper projects as government cuts red tape
item.description: Peru expects to boost annual copper production by about 1 million metric tons within 5 to 6 years through new mining projects, as Chinese and US companies weigh investments amid broader competition for critical minerals in South America, Peru's Energy and Mines Minister told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Marco Aquino
item.content:encoded: Peru expects to boost annual copper production by about 1 million metric tons within 5 to 6 years through new [USN:L6N43H166 TEXT:"mining projects"], as Chinese and US companies weigh investments amid broader competition for critical minerals in South America, Peru's Energy and Mines Minister told Reuters. Peru, the world's third-largest copper producer, expects output to remain between 2.5 million and 2.7 million tons this year, roughly unchanged from 2023 due to declining ore grades and recurring social conflicts, Minister Guillermo Shinno said. The newly elected conservative government of [USN:L6N43Q0ZQ TEXT:"President Keiko Fujimori"] is seeking to reverse that [USN:L1N3WU0PV TEXT:"stagnation"] by cutting red tape. In the two months since the Fujimori administration took office, mining companies have stepped up engagement with the ministry as they seek to revive stalled projects, Shinno said. Companies including from China , Peru's largest copper customer, and from the US as [USN:S0N42V05J TEXT:"Washington"] seeks to expand its footprint in critical mineral supply chains, have expressed interest. "Expectations are enormous. Everyone has been asking questions and coming to the ministry to see how they can move forward with their projects," Shinno said in an interview with Reuters late on Thursday. CUTTING BACK SOME REQUIREMENTS The minister said the government was committed to reducing roughly 100 permitting requirements across the mining sector to attract investment. "We have identified 27 permits that could be eliminated," the minister said. "This is not about lowering environmental standards, but about being rigorous and very clear." About 70% of Peru's $64 billion mining project pipeline is tied to copper, Shinno added. Most of the roughly $7 billion in mining investment expected in 2026 is aimed at sustaining operations or extending mine life, rather than adding significant new output. "With the new projects we have planned, in five or six years we could add another million tons of copper production per year," Shinno said. CHINESE, US FIRMS EYE PROJECTS Among roughly 20 companies that have met with the new administration are Chinese firms such as MMG (1208.HK) , which owns [USN:L6N44G16H TEXT:"Las Bambas"], Chinalco, Shougang and Jinzhao, US-based miners Newmont (NEM.N) and Freeport-McMoRan FCX.N and global mining companies First Quantum (FM.TO) , Barrick (ABX.TO) , Anglo American (AAL.L) and Glencore (GLEN.L) , ministry records show. Shinno said First Quantum wants to advance its La Granja copper project, while Chinalco in July acquired the Los Calatos project in southern Peru, which is undergoing environmental studies ahead of development. First Quantum representatives in Lima did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The government estimates investments of $2.4 billion for La Granja and $655 million for Los Calatos in the coming years. The Toromocho mine, operated by [USN:L1N3YU1NA TEXT:"Chinalco"], and Las Bambas are among Peru's 6 largest copper mines. Shinno said he also expects greater US mining investment as Washington seeks to counter Chinese influence in strategic minerals. The US and Peru signed a critical minerals cooperation agreement in February, which US Secretary of State Marco Rubio highlighted during a [USN:L1N4520UP TEXT:"visit to Peru"] this month as a way to capitalize on new opportunities in the sector. "We hope that more American companies will be encouraged to come," Shinno added.

item.title: Russia says it struck Ukrainian defence industry facilities, vessels
item.description: The Russian defence ministry said on Friday its forces had carried out overnight drone strikes on Ukrainian defence industry facilities, logistics centres and vessels used by Ukraine's armed forces.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Russian defence ministry said on Friday its forces had carried out overnight drone strikes on Ukrainian defence industry facilities, logistics centres and vessels used by Ukraine's armed forces. The ministry said the strikes hit a drone assembly and storage site in the Kyiv region, logistics hubs in the Odesa region and port infrastructure in Reni on the Danube River. It also said Russian forces struck a cargo ship carrying military and dual-use goods to the port of Odesa. The ministry said later on Friday that its forces had struck another cargo vessel in the Odesa region that delivered military supplies to the port of Chornomorsk, a logistics centre used by Ukraine's military and security forces, and a data centre used for processing and transmission of intelligence data. Reuters could not independently verify the statements.

item.title: US Senate approves legislation to address pilot, air traffic control mental health issues
item.description: The US Senate approved bipartisan legislation to modernize regulations on mental health guidance for pilots and air traffic controllers to encourage early disclosure and treatment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US Senate approved bipartisan legislation to modernize regulations on mental health guidance for pilots and air traffic controllers to encourage early disclosure and treatment. Commercial airline pilots often conceal mental health conditions for fear that disclosing therapy or medication, or even just seeking help, could mean having their license pulled, putting themselves and their passengers at risk. The issue drew new attention after an off-duty Alaska Airlines (ALK.N) pilot in late 2023 was charged with trying to disable the engines of a jet in flight and told police afterward he was suffering a nervous breakdown. The legislation, sponsored by Senators John Hoeven and Tammy Duckworth, was approved unanimously late Thursday and aims to encourage pilots and air traffic controllers to seek mental health care, when needed, while reducing the stigma. A separate bill also passed by the Senate requires the FAA to issue accessible, user-friendly guidance on approved medications to ensure pilots or controllers these individuals don't unknowingly take medications that could put their careers in jeopardy. "Their careers should never be threatened because they weren't properly informed about which medications they're allowed to take, or simply sought the mental health care they need," said Duckworth, a Democrat, adding lawmakers aim to "dismantle the dangerous culture of silence surrounding mental health in the aviation industry and ultimately make our skies safer." Pilots face strict rules around medication and can be forced to stop flying for three months if they change antidepressant or anxiety drug dosage levels or medications for mental health issues. Hoeven, a Republican, noted the significant shortage of qualified pilots and air traffic controllers, adding "bureaucratic delays and outdated processes at the FAA keep these professionals from working for prolonged periods when they seek mental health care." The Allied Pilots Association, which represents 17,000 pilots at American Airlines (AAL.O) , praised passage of the bills saying they represent meaningful progress toward modernizing the FAA’s approach to pilot mental health. "For far too long, pilots have faced barriers to seeking care and navigating the medical certification process," APA President Nick Silva said. The FAA which did not immediately comment Friday, convened an expert panel in late 2023 to make recommendations on pilot mental health issues and "to help break down barriers that prevent pilots and air traffic controllers from reporting mental health issues." The report found that about 20% of pilots and controllers who report a mental health issue are initially disqualified from work and it can take more than a year to get approval to use an antidepressant medication.

item.title: Na França, papa Leão 14 alerta que ONU corre risco de se tornar uma “farsa”
item.description: O papa Leão 14 afirmou na sexta-feira que as Nações Unidas e outros organismos multilaterais estão em crise, alertando, em um discurso na sede da Unesco, órgão da ONU para a cultura e a educação, em Paris, que o diálogo internacional corre o risco de se tornar uma “farsa”.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee, Elizabeth Pineau
item.content:encoded: O papa Leão 14 afirmou na sexta-feira que as Nações Unidas e outros organismos multilaterais estão em crise, alertando, em um discurso na sede da Unesco, órgão da ONU para a cultura e a educação, em Paris, que o diálogo internacional corre o risco de se tornar uma “farsa”. O primeiro papa norte-americano, falando durante uma visita à França enquanto uma tensa Assembleia Geral da ONU se desenrola em Nova York, também criticou os líderes mundiais que desrespeitam o Estado de Direito, sem citar nomes. “Em vez de respeitar a lei, aqueles que estão no poder a invocam quando lhes convém e a desconsideram quando lhes impõe restrições, tratando até mesmo a própria justiça como se fosse uma mercadoria a ser comprada e vendida”, disse o pontífice. A ONU e outros grupos multilaterais “estão passando por uma crise de eficácia”, afirmou ele. “O diálogo é visto como um obstáculo à ação, em vez de um recurso para a paz; uma farsa, em vez de uma oportunidade de buscar juntos o bem comum.” Leão, que se tornou papa em maio de 2025, despertou a ira do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, no início do ano, após criticar a guerra contra o Irã. A Assembleia Geral da ONU deste ano, que termina na segunda-feira, tem sido palco de discussões acaloradas. Em um discurso na terça-feira, Trump ameaçou aniquilar o Irã caso o país não concorde com os termos para encerrar a guerra. Na quinta-feira, dezenas de delegados deixaram o plenário enquanto o primeiro-ministro israelense, Benjamin Netanyahu, discursava. Trump anunciou em 2025 que os EUA se retirariam da Unesco. Leão está em uma visita a três cidades da França, onde busca restaurar a reputação da Igreja após escândalos de abuso que causaram comoção em todo o país. PAPA ALERTA PARA RISCOS DA IA O papa, que fez do alerta sobre os riscos da IA uma parte central de seu papado de 16 meses, colocou a questão no centro de sua visita à França, a primeira de um papa em quase 20 anos. Na manhã desta sexta-feira, ele exortou o mundo a reconsiderar o desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial, alertando em um discurso aos líderes franceses que a IA poderia criar um futuro em que “um paraíso das máquinas” assumisse o controle da Terra. “Se quisermos evitar perder nossa humanidade em meio a um ‘paraíso das máquinas’ que invade e condiciona nossa vida cotidiana, há uma necessidade urgente de educação em discernimento ético”, disse ele, falando sob os tetos dourados do Palácio do Eliseu. MENSAGEM DE PAZ Leão foi recebido no aeroporto de Orly, em Paris, sob um céu azul límpido, pelo presidente Emmanuel Macron e sua esposa Brigitte, além de crianças que cantaram para ele e pediram autógrafos. Durante sua visita de quatro dias, ele viajará ao famoso santuário católico de Lourdes, no sudoeste, e a Metz, na fronteira com a Alemanha. Ao dizer aos repórteres no avião a caminho de Paris que vinha para transmitir uma mensagem de paz, Leão acrescentou: “É uma mensagem que, neste momento, como todos sabemos, é particularmente importante.” A França, uma nação secular onde a separação entre Igreja e Estado está consagrada em uma lei de 1905, tem testemunhado um declínio constante na filiação à Igreja Católica durante o período do pós-guerra, refletindo uma tendência observada em outros países tradicionalmente católicos.

item.title: La ONU amplía la lista de empresas vinculadas a los asentamientos israelíes
item.description: La Oficina de Derechos Humanos de Naciones Unidas publicó el viernes una lista en la que se añaden 61 empresas más que operan en los asentamientos israelíes de Cisjordania, que este organismo internacional considera ilegales.
item.dc:creator: Emma Farge
item.content:encoded: La Oficina de Derechos Humanos de Naciones Unidas publicó el viernes una lista en la que se añaden 61 empresas más que operan en los asentamientos israelíes de Cisjordania, que este organismo internacional considera ilegales. La base de datos es un asunto muy delicado, ya que las empresas podrían ser objeto de boicots o desinversiones para presionar a Israel por la expansión de los asentamientos en el territorio, donde viven más de tres millones de palestinos. La base de datos, publicada por primera vez en 2020, incluye ahora 214 empresas, en su mayoría de Israel, pero también de otros 10 países, entre ellos Francia, Alemania, China y Estados Unidos. Entre las empresas recién añadidas se encuentran el fabricante israelí de pesticidas ADAMA, que forma parte del grupo chino Syngenta, la sociedad de inversión inmobiliaria con sede en Israel Alony Hetz y la española Salvat Logística. Se suman así a empresas como la agencia de viajes Expedia y la plataforma de alquiler de viviendas Airbnb, que ya figuraban en la lista. Israel, que considera que Cisjordania es un territorio en disputa y no ocupado, ha afirmado anteriormente que la lista difama de forma injusta a las empresas que operan legalmente. "Se trata de un mecanismo sesgado, creado por un organismo profundamente defectuoso con una mayoría automática en contra de Israel", dijo el viernes la misión diplomática israelí, alegando que la base de datos se creó para "perseguir" al Estado judío. Se ha producido un aumento de los ataques de los colonos contra los palestinos a medida que proliferan los asentamientos, lo que ha llevado a Reino Unido, Francia y Canadá a bloquear este mes las importaciones procedentes de los asentamientos.

item.title: Prestigioso premio Goncourt de Francia retira novela tras acusaciones de uso de IA contra su autor
item.description: Los organizadores del prestigioso premio literario Goncourt anunciaron el viernes la retirada de su lista preliminar una novela de gran éxito del autor haitiano-canadiense Thelyson Orelien, tras las acusaciones de que recurrió a la inteligencia artificial para escribirla.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los organizadores del prestigioso premio literario Goncourt anunciaron el viernes la retirada de su lista preliminar una novela de gran éxito del autor haitiano-canadiense Thelyson Orelien, tras las acusaciones de que recurrió a la inteligencia artificial para escribirla. Orelien negó haber utilizado IA para escribir "C'était ça ou mourir" ("Era eso o morir"), mientras las acusaciones desencadenaban un debate sobre raza, mérito literario y originalidad que ha agitado al establishment literario francés. Las acusaciones sobre el uso de la IA las lanzó esta semana una cuenta poco conocida de la red social X llamada "Balance ton Claude". El ensayista Samuel Fitoussi reivindicó más tarde la autoría de la cuenta, afirmando que la gestionaba junto con otras personas no identificadas. A las acusaciones sobre la IA les siguieron informes que apuntaban a que Orelien había cometido plagio en obras anteriores. La Presse señaló que un relato corto de Orelien de 2012 había plagiado pasajes de un libro del autor francés Louis Pauwels, mientras que un artículo de opinión de 2013 copiaba del periódico The Philippine Star. Orelien aún no ha respondido a esas acusaciones y no contestó a una solicitud de comentarios el viernes. La Academia Goncourt, con sede en París, declaró que había tomado nota de las acusaciones de uso de IA y de plagio, y que había decidido retirar su novela "para preservar la integridad del Premio Goncourt y la de la Academia, cuya función principal es promover y honrar la literatura escrita por mujeres y hombres". La Academia afirmó que espera que su decisión muestre su total oposición a la "creación de textos generados con la ayuda de la IA" y añadió que no hará más comentarios hasta el 6 de octubre, fecha en la que anunciará su lista de finalistas. La primera novela del autor, nacido en Haití, narra la historia de un migrante haitiano que viaja hacia el norte a través de América Latina antes de llegar a Canadá. La obra ha ganado numerosos premios literarios y estaba previsto que se tradujera a varios idiomas. Sus editoriales francesa y canadiense ofrecieron inicialmente a Orelien todo su apoyo ante las acusaciones relacionadas con la IA. El viernes no respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios. Balance ton Claude afirmó que al pasar fragmentos de la novela por la herramienta de detección de IA Pangram se observó que la novela 2había sido escrita casi en su totalidad por inteligencia artificial". Algunos expertos señalan que la fiabilidad de las herramientas de detección de IA es cuestionable.

item.title: Canada's budget deficit over first four months of 2026/27 slightly falls to C$5.14 billion
item.description: OTTAWA, Sept 25 (Reuters) - Canada recorded a slightly lower C$5.14 billion ($3.63 billion) budget deficit for the first four months of the 2026/27 fiscal year as government revenues grew faster than expenditures, the finance ministry said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: OTTAWA, Sept 25 (Reuters) - Canada recorded a slightly lower C$5.14 billion ($3.63 billion) budget deficit for the first four months of the 2026/27 fiscal year as government revenues grew faster than expenditures, the finance ministry said on Friday. By comparison, the deficit in the same period a year earlier had been C$7.79 billion, it said in a statement. Revenues over the four-month period increased by 7.4% largely reflecting higher income from personal and corporate income tax revenues. Expenses grew by 5.1%, driven by transfers for Old Age Security, increased operating costs and other transfer payments. Public debt charges increased by 7.4%, largely reflecting higher average effective interest rates on an increased stock of marketable bonds, the ministry said. On a monthly basis, Canada's deficit increased sharply to C$4.77 billion in July, compared to a C$1.51 billion deficit in July 2025. ($1 = 1.4146 Canadian dollars) (Reporting by Promit Mukherjee, editing by David Ljunggren) ((Reuters Ottawa bureau; david.ljunggren@tr.com )) Keywords: CANADA BUDGET/

item.title: Manchester City, culpable de todos menos uno de los 115 cargos por infracciones: medios
item.description: El Manchester City fue hallado culpable de todas menos una de las 115 presuntas infracciones de las normas financieras de la Premier League, informaron el viernes The Athletic y The Times.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: El Manchester City fue hallado culpable de todas menos una de las 115 presuntas infracciones de las normas financieras de la Premier League, informaron el viernes The Athletic y The Times. Según añaden los medios, se espera que el club presente un recurso. La Premier declinó hacer declaraciones al respecto. "Se trata de un proceso confidencial, no vamos a hacer ningún comentario", indicó un portavoz. El City no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios de Reuters, pero declaró a la BBC que la investigación sobre las acusaciones "sigue en curso". La Premier remitió al City a una comisión independiente en febrero de 2023 por presuntas infracciones de las normas financieras que abarcan las temporadas 2009-10 a 2022-23. El club ha negado sistemáticamente haber cometido irregularidades. Entre las acusaciones más graves estaba que el City no había facilitado en ninguna de las temporadas comprendidas entre 2009-10 y 2017-18 información financiera precisa que ofreciera una "imagen fiel" de los ingresos, incluidos los ingresos por patrocinios, y los costos operativos. El City contrató al abogado David Pannick para que dirigiera su defensa, mientras que la Premier estuvo representada por Adam Lewis KC, según los medios británicos. La vista comenzó el 16 de septiembre de 2024 y concluyó casi tres meses después, el 6 de diciembre. El caso fue juzgado por una comisión independiente compuesta por tres jueces designados por el presidente independiente del panel judicial de la Premier League. El City fue sancionado con dos años de inhabilitación para participar en la Liga de Campeones por la UEFA, el organismo rector del fútbol europeo, en 2020, tras constatarse que había sobrevalorado sus ingresos por patrocinios entre 2012 y 2016. Sin embargo, el club recurrió con éxito ante el Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS), que anuló la sanción. Desde que el Abu Dhabi United Group del jeque Mansour compró el club en 2008, el City ha ganado ocho títulos de la Premier League, la Liga de Campeones, cuatro Copas de Inglaterra y siete Copas de la Liga. El City lidera la Premier esta temporada tras ganar sus cinco primeros partidos.

item.title: Trump sees no urgency for Canada deal as trade dispute deepens, USTR says
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration is comfortable maintaining its trade standoff with Canada even as new US import bans on Canadian products take effect next week and Washington threatens 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, parts and steel from January, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump 's administration is comfortable maintaining its trade standoff with Canada even as new US import bans on Canadian products take effect next week and Washington threatens 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, parts and steel from January, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Friday. His comments to CNBC signal Washington sees little need to compromise despite a deepening dispute that has strained relations between the longtime allies, triggered retaliation on both sides of the border and raised fresh questions about the future of the US-Mexico-Canada trade agreement. The looming US import bans are on a broad range of Canadian goods, including alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and dairy products. The January increase on tariffs to 50% could carry significant consequences for North American auto production. Canada's own retaliatory tariffs on US goods took effect earlier this month. Canadian tariffs followed 50% tariffs that the US imposed on some $20 billion of Canadian goods last month, after several rounds of negotiations collapsed. "We're still getting what we need from them in terms of oil, gas, potash, all of these things. We're shipping (agricultural products) back and forth across the border, so there's still a lot of strong trade between the two countries," Greer told CNBC. "We're comfortable with where we are. ... They call us now and then, and we have good conversations about potential deals. But it's not – there's no urgency on our side, I would say." The Canadian Embassy in Washington did not immediately comment. The breakdown has widened a rift between the longtime allies, who have blamed each other for the failed talks, spurred Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to urge a further shift away from Canada's biggest trading partner, and cast doubt on the viability of the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement. Some experts think the Trump administration wants to first reach a deal with Mexico, which could give the US more leverage to get a better agreement with Canada. The next round of talks with Mexico could occur in October, Mexican officials said this week.

item.title: Anvisa proíbe propaganda da caneta Semavy
item.description: A Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) anunciou nesta sexta-feira que a Mantecorp, do grupo Hypera , não pode promover diretamente ao público a caneta de semaglutida Semavy, citando que a publicidade de medicamentos de tarja vermelha ou preta é proibida no Brasil.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) anunciou nesta sexta-feira que a Mantecorp, do grupo Hypera (HYPE3.SA) , não pode promover diretamente ao público a caneta de semaglutida Semavy, citando que a publicidade de medicamentos de tarja vermelha ou preta é proibida no Brasil. "A Anvisa constatou a realização de propaganda do medicamento, por meio de painéis eletrônicos localizados no Aeroporto de Congonhas, no site do produto e em contas de redes sociais", afirmou a agência em comunicado à imprensa. As ações da Hypera recuavam 0,6%, cotadas a R$24,47, às 11h06, enquanto o Ibovespa (.BVSP) tinha queda de 0,9%. Segundo a Anvisa, a legislação apenas permite a propaganda de medicamentos que sejam isentos de prescrição médica, e a divulgação de drogas com tarja vermelha ou preta só pode ser feita a médicos, dentistas ou farmacêuticos.

item.title: BOLSA EUA Otimismo com IA ameniza preocupações com petróleo e rendimentos e Wall Street sobe
item.description: Os principais índices de Wall Street avançavam nesta sexta-feira, com o otimismo em relação à IA impulsionando o sentimento apesar dos preços elevados do petróleo e do aumento dos rendimentos dos Treasuries, enquanto os investidores acompanhavam os esforços para garantir um acordo que ponha fim ao conflito no Oriente Médio.
item.dc:creator: Johann Cherian, Avinash P
item.content:encoded: Os principais índices de Wall Street avançavam nesta sexta-feira, com o otimismo em relação à IA impulsionando o sentimento apesar dos preços elevados do petróleo e do aumento dos rendimentos dos Treasuries, enquanto os investidores acompanhavam os esforços para garantir um acordo que ponha fim ao conflito no Oriente Médio. As ações da Microsoft (MSFT.O) subiam 3% e davam o maior impulso ao S&P 500 depois que a gigante do software revelou vários novos recursos em seu aplicativo Copilot, incluindo uma ferramenta de programação e um agente de IA sempre ativo. As fabricantes de chips Micron (MU.O) e Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) ganhavam cerca de 1% cada, enquanto a Nvidia (NVDA.O) registrava alta marginal. O otimismo em relação à IA foi um fator importante nesta semana, impulsionado pelo Muse, da Meta (META.O) , e seu dispositivo integrado, o Charm, que vêm ganhando força entre os jovens consumidores. Alguns analistas apontaram isso como resultado dos fortes gastos com a tecnologia. “A quantidade de dinheiro que está sendo injetada na economia por meio de investimentos em IA é simplesmente enorme, e ainda nem vimos a parte relacionada à produtividade”, disse Jamie Cox, sócio-gerente do Harris Financial Group. “O mercado está levando um pouco disso em consideração na avaliação, e essa é uma das razões pelas quais realmente não se vê uma grande liquidação.” O Índice Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) subia 0,44%, para 51.576,71 pontos, enquanto o S&P 500 (.SPX) avançava 0,29%, para 7.726,62 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) tinha alta de 0,41%, para 27.048,75 pontos. Oito dos 11 setores do S&P 500 registravam queda, mas isso era compensado por um ganho de 1% no setor de tecnologia (.SPLRCT) . Tanto o S&P 500 quanto o Nasdaq (.IXIC) estavam a caminho de registrarem altas semanais. Uma notícia de que os negociadores dos EUA e do Irã continuavam a explorar um caminho gradual para sair do conflito, o que envolveria Teerã reabrindo o Estreito de Ormuz e Washington suspendendo seu bloqueio econômico, ajudava a melhorar o ânimo do mercado. O otimismo, no entanto, era limitado pelas preocupações com a inflação, impulsionadas pelos conflitos prolongados no Irã e na Ucrânia e pelo aumento vertiginoso da dívida pública. Os preços do petróleo Brent oscilavam acima de US$ 100 por barril, e o rendimento do Treasury de 10 anos estavam em 5,1%. Os operadores agora estimam uma probabilidade de 64% de que o Federal Reserve aumentará a taxa de juros em pelo menos 25 pontos-base em outubro, ante cerca de 50% mais cedo nesta semana, segundo a ferramenta FedWatch do CME Group.

item.title: Fed's Schmid: Need to understand if AI "ecosystem" getting too big to fail
item.description: Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said that as the artificial intelligence boom unfolds it will be important for the Fed to understand if the network of firms and contracts developing in the industry is becoming so large it is too big to fail.
item.dc:creator: Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said that as the artificial intelligence boom unfolds it will be important for the Fed to understand if the network of firms and contracts developing in the industry is becoming so large it is too big to fail. "Where we have to start to really synthesize what's happening in the AI and the data center build-out is are we moving to a too-big-to-fail AI ecosystem," he said, referring to the need for public bailouts of major financial institutions during the 2007 to 2009 financial crisis because of their size and influence on the broader economy. "You worry a little bit about how do we understand what's inside. ... Is there anything systemic?" he asked.

item.title: New York Yacht Club plots biennial women's international event
item.description: With a mix of Olympians, America's Cup sailors, national champions and amateurs, interest in the inaugural New York Yacht Club Women's International Championship last week was so strong that its organisers are already planning a follow-up in 2028.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Smith
item.content:encoded: With a mix of Olympians, [USN:L8N45F18Y TEXT:"America's Cup"] sailors, national champions and amateurs, interest in the inaugural New York Yacht Club Women's International Championship last week was so strong that its organisers are already planning a follow-up in 2028. "Having seen the success of this one, we're committed for 2028. We will definitely do it again," NYYC Commodore Clare Harrington said during the 20-team event, which ended in victory for a US crew skippered by Megan Grapengeter-Rudnick. Harrington said the quality of the 200 skippers and sailors who committed to the event was impressive, citing New Zealand's Megan Thomson, who had just completed the [USN:L6N4520YB TEXT:"Ocean Race Atlantic"], as one example. "She (Thomson) finished the race in Europe and then flew right back over here to get on the IC37. So it's really pretty cool," Harrington told Reuters in a video interview. Thomson's team ended up 14th in the regatta, in which crews competed in the NYYC's fleet of identical IC37s, a 37-foot keelboat which the club describes as "a powerful, sporty platform that rewards cohesive crew work and athleticism". For Harrington, who in 2025 was elected as the first female commodore in the NYYC's 182-year history, getting this year's women-only event onto the water in Newport, Rhode Island, was "kind of an experiment". "We kept the entry fee at $5,000 for this championship because we just weren't sure how this was going to play out," Harrington said, adding that this compared with around $35,000 for the club's long-established Invitational Cup. Financial backing was critical to staging the regatta, with the cost of sails alone totalling around $600,000, and NYYC was able to sign up major sponsors including State Street Investment Management SPY, Rolex and Helly Hansen. NYYC also had what Harrington described as a "beautiful, spectacular" trophy specially made in Rhode Island by Tiffany. Harrington said she was shocked and "beyond honoured" when she was made commodore. "But I never at any point felt that I was appointed, nominated because I'm a woman," she said, adding: "I would never have accepted it if I thought that was the case". "I didn't come out of thin air. I paid my dues. I've worked hard for the club for many years," she said, pointing out that she had for several years done "probably one of the most difficult jobs at the club" as chair of the race committee. "I am the first woman, so I feel like there have been a lot of eyes on me," she added.

item.title: Data center IPO hopefuls brave tougher market as investor scrutiny grows
item.description: Data center operator DayOne is pushing ahead with its plans to go public as soon as November, according to three people familiar with the matter, even as higher interest rates and setbacks elsewhere in the data center ecosystem threaten to narrow the window for companies to tap the IPO market.
item.dc:creator: Echo Wang, Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: Data center operator DayOne is pushing ahead with its plans to go public as soon as November, according to three people familiar with the matter, even as higher interest rates and setbacks elsewhere in the data center ecosystem threaten to narrow the window for companies to tap the IPO market. The Singapore-based company develops and operates data centers for cloud and AI customers. It plans to make its filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission public in mid-October and list in November, the people said, speaking anonymously to discuss confidential matters. The plans, including the timing of the IPO, are subject to change, the people cautioned. DayOne declined to comment. DayOne's IPO intentions follow two setbacks for data center operators this week: the delay of [USN:L6N45E108 TEXT:"SB Energy's"] expected IPO and news of [USN:L4N45G11W TEXT:"a "][USN:L4N45G11W TEXT:"dispute"] centering on Oracle and Blue Owl (OWL.N) that could delay a data center project in New Mexico. The contrast highlights how the market for AI infrastructure is maturing after years of strong investor enthusiasm. Companies with diversified customers and greater visibility into demand can still attract interest, while projects that rely heavily on a single AI customer or require large amounts of capital upfront face greater scrutiny. "The dividing line is whether demand is contracted and already energised, or only planned," said Ke Yan, head of research at Singapore-based investment research firm Shenton Research. With power now the key constraint, investors favour operators with secured power supply, a large share of contracted capacity already operating or nearing completion, and long-dated take-or-pay contracts, he said. Investor scrutiny is intensifying as a growing pipeline of companies head toward the public markets, with data center developers and operators including Switch, Vantage Data Centers and CyrusOne exploring or preparing IPOs. Switch has filed confidentially for an IPO, and is expected to launch its offering following DayOne, one of the people said. Switch did not respond to a request for comments. A MORE DIVERSIFIED OFFERING DayOne's geographic diversification and the fact it has operational data centers, not just ones under development, have helped distinguish it from some rivals in the eyes of investors, one of the people said. The company, backed by investors like Coatue and Hillhouse, raised $4.5 billion in a Series C funding round that closed in June. It could seek to raise as much as $5 billion in the IPO at a valuation of about $20 billion, [USN:L4N3Z90QB TEXT:"Reuters has reported"]. It has secured about 2.1 gigawatts of capacity bookings and operates across Asia-Pacific and Europe, including Malaysia, Hong Kong, Japan, Finland and Spain, according to its website. Meanwhile, SoftBank-backed SB Energy has postponed plans to formally market its IPO this week as it works to address additional questions from the US Securities and Exchange Commission. There are also investor concerns over the valuation it is seeking and its reliance on OpenAI as a major customer, one of the three people familiar with the matter and another person said. Discussions around the IPO have centered on a valuation of about $60 billion, one of the people added. SB Energy declined to comment. There have been various dealings between SoftBank, SB Energy, its main data center customer OpenAI and OpenAI's chip supplier Nvidia in recent months. Nvidia (NVDA.O) has [USN:L6N44E0NJ TEXT:"agreed"] to provide a guarantee of up to $105 billion to help OpenAI lease the Ohio data center being developed by SB Energy, while also investing $1.5 billion in SB Energy. OpenAI backer SoftBank is [USN:L1N45F065 TEXT:"taking investor orders"] for a $10 billion dollar-denominated debt deal to help fund its OpenAI investments. The company previously took a loan backed by the OpenAI stake. AI SPENDING FACES CLOSER SCRUTINY The cost of financing the AI buildout is coming under greater pressure. AI-related capital spending by the six biggest US technology companies is projected to reach around $1 trillion in 2027, according to Moody’s. [USN:S0N44V008 TEXT:"Higher interest rates"] make it more expensive to finance facilities whose returns may take years to materialize, while [USN:L4N4341D3 TEXT:"investors"] are demanding greater visibility into the customers and cash flows that will support those investments. For developers relying on debt, contracted revenue from creditworthy customers is crucial to servicing that debt as they fund costly AI-ready facilities, including high-density racks and liquid-cooling systems, said Neil Bear-Hetherington, director of data centre capital markets, Asia Pacific, at CBRE. For data center developers, that makes the identity and financial strength of their customers increasingly important to investors evaluating projects that can require billions of dollars of upfront investment. For companies preparing to go public, a less forgiving IPO market and greater scrutiny of AI infrastructure create an incentive to move quickly while investor demand is available. "The earlier the better. Uncertainty is what hurts data-center models. Investors in data centers are looking for yield and growth together, and uncertainty weighs on both, since it raises the cost of the debt that supports the yield and delays the grid and financing that growth depends on," said Yan of Shenton Research.

item.title: Man City found guilty on all but one of 115 charges, reports say
item.description: Manchester City have been found guilty of all but one of the 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, the Athletic and the Times reported on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester City have been found guilty of all but one of the 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, the Athletic and the Times reported on Friday. The club are expected to appeal, the reports added. The Premier League declined to comment. "It’s a confidential process, we’re not commenting at all," a spokesperson said. City maintained the case had not yet been concluded. "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality," the club said in a statement to British media. "As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023. "The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence." If confirmed, the guilty verdict would represent one of the most significant rulings in English football history and mark a major development in a case that has overshadowed the league for more than three years. The proceedings have raised questions about financial regulation, competitive integrity and how the league enforces its rules against its most successful clubs. ALLEGATIONS SPANNING MORE THAN A DECADE The Premier League referred City to an independent commission in February 2023 over [USN:L4N34M29T TEXT:"alleged breaches"] of financial rules spanning the 2009-10 to 2022-23 seasons. The club have consistently denied wrongdoing. Among the most serious allegations was that City failed in each season from 2009-10 to 2017-18 to provide accurate financial information giving a "true and fair view" of revenues, including sponsorship income, and operating costs. City hired lawyer David Pannick to lead their defence, while the Premier League was represented by Adam Lewis KC, according to British media reports. The hearing began on September 16, 2024, and concluded nearly three months later on December 6. The case was heard by an independent commission composed of three people appointed by the independent chair of the Premier League Judicial Panel. City were banned from the Champions League for two years by European football's governing body UEFA in 2020 after being found to have overstated sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016. The club, however, successfully appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which overturned the ban. Since Sheikh Mansour’s Abu Dhabi United Group bought the club in 2008, City have won eight Premier League titles, the Champions League, four FA Cups and seven League Cups. City top the Premier League after winning each of their opening five matches. The stakes are particularly high because other clubs have already faced sporting sanctions for breaching financial regulations. Everton were docked a total of eight points during the 2023-24 season after two separate breaches of the Premier League's Profitability and Sustainability Rules, while Nottingham Forest were deducted four points for a breach of the same rules in March 2024. Newcastle United narrowly avoided potential sanctions after selling players before a June 30, 2024, financial reporting deadline to comply with spending regulations. The allegations against City are far broader and cover more than a decade, making the case unprecedented in scale. Lawyers, club executives and supporters across the league have spent years awaiting a verdict.

item.title: EEUU no ve urgencia para acuerdo con Canadá mientras se agrava disputa comercial
item.description: El Gobierno de Estados Unidos no tiene ningún problema en mantener su disputa comercial con Canadá, incluso aunque la próxima semana empiece a aplicar nuevas prohibiciones a la importación de productos canadienses, dijo el viernes el jefe de la representación comercial estadounidense (USTR), Jamieson Greer, a la cadena CNBC.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno de Estados Unidos no tiene ningún problema en mantener su disputa comercial con Canadá, incluso aunque la próxima semana empiece a aplicar nuevas prohibiciones a la importación de productos canadienses, dijo el viernes el jefe de la representación comercial estadounidense (USTR), Jamieson Greer, a la cadena CNBC. Sus declaraciones indican que Washington no ve mucha necesidad de ceder, pese a una disputa cada vez más profunda que ha tensado las relaciones entre estos aliados de larga data, ha desencadenado represalias a ambos lados de la frontera y ha suscitado nuevas dudas sobre el futuro del acuerdo comercial entre Estados Unidos, México y Canadá (TMEC). Las inminentes prohibiciones de importación de Estados Unidos afectan a una amplia gama de productos canadienses, entre los que se incluyen bebidas alcohólicas, motocicletas y productos lácteos. Además, la administración del presidente Donald Trump amenaza con aplicar aranceles del 50% a automóviles, piezas y acero canadienses a partir de enero, un escenario que podría generar consecuencias significativas para la producción automovilística norteamericana. Los aranceles de Canadá sobre los productos estadounidenses entraron en vigor a principios de mes, en represalia por las tarifas del 50% que Washington impuso a unos 20.000 millones de dólares en productos canadienses, después de que fracasaran varias rondas de negociaciones. "Seguimos obteniendo de ellos lo que necesitamos en cuanto a petróleo, gas, potasa y todo eso. Estamos enviando (productos agrícolas) de un lado a otro de la frontera, por lo que sigue habiendo un comercio muy intenso entre los dos países", declaró Greer a la CNBC. "Estamos tranquilos con la situación actual (...) Nos llaman de vez en cuando y mantenemos buenas conversaciones sobre posibles acuerdos. Pero no (...) no hay urgencia por nuestra parte, diría yo", agregó. La embajada de Canadá en Washington no hizo comentarios de inmediato. El fracaso de las negociaciones ha agravado la brecha entre ambos aliados, que se culpan mutuamente del fracaso de las conversaciones, lo que llevó al primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, a instar a un mayor distanciamiento del principal socio comercial de Ottawa y ha sembrado dudas sobre la viabilidad del TMEC. Algunos expertos creen que la administración Trump quiere llegar primero a un acuerdo con México, lo que podría darle más poder de negociación para conseguir un acuerdo más favorable con Canadá. La próxima ronda de negociaciones con México podría tener lugar en octubre, según han declarado esta semana funcionarios mexicanos.

item.title: US harvest delays send soy processors scrambling for supplies
item.description: Soybean processors in the western US Midwest are offering hefty premiums for immediate deliveries of the oilseed as persistent rains delay the early harvest, tightening supplies and forcing some plants to scale back production, according to interviews with grain merchandisers and publicly reported company data.
item.dc:creator: P.J. Huffstutter, Julie Ingwersen
item.content:encoded: Soybean processors in the western US Midwest are offering hefty premiums for immediate deliveries of the oilseed as persistent rains delay the early harvest, tightening supplies and forcing some plants to scale back production, according to interviews with grain merchandisers and publicly reported company data. The scramble for soybeans has sent cash prices soaring, creating an unexpected windfall for farmers able to harvest their crops and get them to market, or sell off the last of their old crops. US soybean processing capacity has expanded in recent years, largely due to rising demand for biofuel. The USDA has projected that processors will crush a record-high 2.78 billion bushels of soybeans in the current crop year, a brisk pace prompted by [USN:S0N3WX040 TEXT:"robust profit margins"]. Yet some crushers have struggled to keep operating this month, analysts said, as supplies from last year's harvest dwindle while the 2026 harvest is off to a slow start. Charlie Sernatinger, executive vice president of Marex, said there were "a ton of crush plants out there gasping for beans," with potential for soybeans being shipped from eastern regions. RAINS SLOW HARVEST Many growers are unable to take advantage of the sudden price spike. Late-summer rains have left fields too muddy to support harvesting equipment and slowed crops' natural dry-down process, and forecasts called for more showers through next week. Iowa farmer Roger Cerven sold off the last of his old-crop soybeans recently, hauling them more than 50 miles despite soaring fuel costs, to Bunge's soybean processing plant in Council Bluffs, Iowa. The processor at the time was offering a 65-cent premium on every bushel delivered. On Thursday, the premium reached 85 cents per bushel for soybeans delivered through Saturday. The soybean crop in Cerven's fields in Montgomery County, southwest Iowa, is weeks away from harvest, even if the ground were dry. Friends and neighbors are in the same situation, he said. "I don't know anyone who has soybeans to sell right now," Cerven said. SUDDEN PRICE SURGE The sudden surge in cash prices contrasts with conditions a year ago, when local soybean prices were under pressure amid renewed US-China trade tensions and a halt in purchases by the world's largest soybean importer. On Thursday, global agribusiness giant Cargill was bidding $1 a bushel over the price of Chicago Board of Trade November soybean futures for beans delivered to its Sioux City, Iowa, crushing plant on Thursday or Friday, according to the company's website. That bid translated to a flat price of $14.17-1/2 a bushel. For deliveries on Saturday, however, Cargill's bid drops to 15 cents below November futures — a swing that underscores the demand for immediate soybean supplies. Similar short-term premiums were also offered at soy processing sites in Iowa and Minnesota operated by agribusiness Archer-Daniels-Midland, cooperative CHS Inc and Iowa-based Shell Rock Soy Processing. SCALING BACK CRUSH Some plants have already scaled back their operations crushing whole soybeans into soymeal, used in livestock feed, and soyoil, used for foods and biofuels, because they have been unable to secure sufficient soybean supplies, according to two grain merchandisers interviewed by Reuters. As a result, Cargill plants in Cedar Rapids, Iowa Falls and Sioux City, Iowa, did not post offers for soymeal due to a lack of supplies, merchandisers said. The shortfall in the cash soy market has rippled into the futures market as well. CBOT October soymeal futures surged on Thursday to a life-of-contract high and traded at an unusual inverse, or premium, to December soymeal futures for the first time in more than two years. Officials from Shell Rock Soy Processing declined to comment on Thursday. Cargill, CHS and ADM could not immediately be reached for comment. STRUGGLES ACROSS REGION Soy processors in the central and eastern Midwest have struggled with harvest delays as well, prompting some to woo farmers with higher prices. Bunge Global SA's soy plant in Decatur, Indiana, raised its soybean bid by 20 cents on Thursday, to 25 cents over November futures, for loads delivered by Friday. Bunge could not be reached for comment. Excessive rains across central Indiana have muddied fields and prevented farmers from harvesting. Local corn and soybean farmers are reporting that heavy rains in August left their crops heavily saturated, and have slowed down the natural dry-down process — which in turn is pushing back their crops' maturity dates by several weeks.

item.title: TV networks resume covering White House as legal battle continues
item.description: US television networks resumed their coverage of President Donald Trump's White House events on Friday, amid an ongoing court fight over the administration's decision to block CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the presidential grounds.
item.dc:creator: Susan Heavey
item.content:encoded: US television networks resumed their coverage of President Donald Trump's White House events on Friday, amid an ongoing court fight over the administration's decision to block CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the presidential grounds. The White House television press pool on Friday aired video of Chinese President Xi Jinping's arrival at the White House for tea as well as the two leaders' [USN:L8N45G1YG TEXT:"tour of the National Archives"], which houses the US Constitution. CNN along with ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC share the costs of covering the president and rotate coverage, providing pool footage to other outlets. The other networks' refusal to set up cameras in solidarity had meant there was no pool coverage of Xi's visit to Washington until Friday. Trump has long used the press as a platform and punching bag, and since returning to office his administration has taken an aggressive stance against major news outlets, including limiting access to the Oval Office for some. Trump declined to answer questions from reporters on China and Iran, his media ban and a controversial new government television ad as Xi arrived at the White House on Friday. "We appreciate the fair coverage. It's been very fair. We appreciate it," Trump later told reporters alongside Xi. The White House did not respond to a request for comment. UNPRECEDENTED CAMPAIGN Trump had [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"banned the three news outlets"] from the White House complex over coverage he asserted was false or negative. Their access was reinstated on Thursday after a federal judge deemed [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"the ban"] likely unconstitutional and ordered their access to be immediately restored. CNN, MS NOW and Politico sued Trump and other members of his administration, saying the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations, including Reuters, later filed a legal brief supporting the three news outlets and highlighting press access' central role to democracy. Trump's campaign against the media has been unprecedented. Upending decades of tradition, his White House has denied basic access to many major news organizations, launched personal attacks on journalists and filed multiple lawsuits against news organizations. On Thursday, Trump made a joke to photographers in the Oval Office about the Chinese having the friendliest press corps, as he welcomed Xi to the White House. Trump and his fellow Republicans, who are seeking to maintain their narrow majorities in Congress, have decried communism on the campaign trail before the midterms and [USN:L6N45B01C TEXT:"have falsely accused Democrats"] of embracing communist ideology. Xi became head of the Chinese Communist Party in 2012. While the White House on Thursday told the court it had reinstated CNN, MS NOW and Politico's access, CNN and MS NOW later said some of their journalists were denied access to cover Xi's arrival for the White House state dinner, according to the Washington Post. A lawyer for the three outlets in court this week warned that the White House could again try to revoke the outlets' White House access as the current litigation continues. David Ellison, CEO of Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) which is seeking to merge with CNN-parent Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) , attended the [USN:L6N45G1DV TEXT:"Trump-Xi state dinner"] Thursday night. Critics have raised concerns about Paramount-owned CBS News tailoring coverage to favor Trump although Ellison has promised to create an [USN:L4N45E0EO TEXT:"editorial independence board"] for both CBS and CNN as part of the deal.

item.title: Russell storms to dominant Baku pole as championship leader Antonelli crashes
item.description: George Russell gave himself the best chance of putting a dent in Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli’s runaway championship lead as he seized pole after a rare mistake sent the Italian crashing out of qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Takle
item.content:encoded: George Russell gave himself the best chance of putting a dent in Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli’s runaway championship lead as he seized pole after a rare mistake sent the Italian crashing out of qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The 28-year-old Briton appeared to be streets ahead of his rivals with his one minute 42.526 second lap, half a second quicker than his own previous benchmark, eclipsing his closest challenger, Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, by 0.837 seconds. “It’s been a while, so it definitely feels good,” said Russell after taking the 12th pole position of his career, his fifth of the season but first since the Austrian Grand Prix at the end of June. “It’s probably the biggest margin in my whole career, even including F2, F3 days. So, the lap felt really sweet. “The car’s been feeling great this weekend and on a track like this, when you can hook it up like that, it feels really amazing,” added the Briton. Russell trails Antonelli by 81 points after 14 rounds. He has looked in commanding form all weekend, however, with only four-times champion Max Verstappen denying him a practice clean sweep by just 0.099 seconds. Already one of the favourites heading into qualifying, Russell's path to pole was smoothed by Antonelli’s exit. The 20-year-old, who went into the weekend gunning for a third successive win and ninth of the season so far, clobbered the barrier lining the inside of the first corner in the opening phase of qualifying. The contact broke his suspension and forced him to park up. He will start 16th. “It’s a good way to come back to earth and to remind myself that I need to be on top of it every time because otherwise I do these mistakes and a very stupid one,” said Antonelli. The Italian’s exit left the door open for other rivals to challenge Russell. RIVALS STRUGGLE McLaren appeared like they might stage a late resurgence as they did at Spain’s Madring two weeks ago but the best they could manage was third for Australian Oscar Piastri. World champion Lando Norris locked up on his final attempt and ended up fifth. Verstappen also faded from contention, qualifying 1.5 seconds off the pace in eighth after being hobbled by power unit problems throughout qualifying and a yellow flag on his final run. However his Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar, returning from an injury-enforced three-race break, came an impressive fourth. Ferrari's seven-times champion Lewis Hamilton was only sixth ahead of Alpine's Pierre Gasly. Carlos Sainz made it through to the final phase of qualifying in his updated Williams but will drop five places after being hit with a penalty for failing to slow for yellow flags. That will move Alpine's Franco Colapinto up to ninth with Haas racer Oliver Bearman rounding out the top 10. Mexican Sergio Perez was also hit with a three-place grid drop for impeding Piastri. But the Cadillac driver could still end up starting 20th, where he qualified, with Aston Martin pair Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll carrying hefty power unit related penalties. The Baku street circuit is known for throwing up unpredictable races. There have been seven different winners in the nine races it has hosted, while only three races at the track have been won from pole. The Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the first of a "triple header" of races on consecutive weekends, is being run on Saturday this year with the country marking its Remembrance Day on Sunday.

item.title: EU vote on Tesla's supervised self-driving system pushed back
item.description: An expected European Union vote on allowing Tesla's supervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) system across the bloc has been delayed from October, with the next apparent opportunity for a decision not before December, according to an agenda published on the EU's website.
item.dc:creator: Marie Mannes
item.content:encoded: An expected European Union vote on allowing Tesla's supervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) system across the bloc has been delayed from October, with the next apparent opportunity for a decision not before December, according to an agenda published on the EU's website. Dutch regulator RDW [USN:S8N3YL09Y TEXT:"approved"] the system in April, with [USN:L1N41Q0KT TEXT:"Belgium"] and a handful of [USN:L8N45D165 TEXT:"other"] countries following suit RDW is also proposing that the software be approved across the bloc Tesla said on September 1 in a post on X that an EU-wide [USN:L6N41E0C3 TEXT:"vote"] could potentially happen on October 6 However, the agenda for an October 6 meeting of the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV), which brings together representatives of EU member states and the European Commission, lists only a "continuation of discussions" on the Dutch request for an Article 39 authorisation, with 25 minutes allocated to the discussion RDW told Reuters it would not speculate on the discussion, the vote or any potential outcome, Tesla did not respond to a request for comment The committee has already discussed Tesla's request at two previous meetings. The next scheduled TCMV meeting after October is in December, making that the earliest apparent opportunity for a vote based on the current agenda An EU-wide rollout requires support by a "qualified majority" of 15 of the EU's 27 member states, representing 65% of the bloc's population Several EU countries, including Sweden, have [USN:L6N41E09R TEXT:"expressed concerns"] about FSD exceeding speed limits, while countries that approved it say drivers remain responsible for complying with traffic laws The same committee approved Ford's (F.N) BlueCruise [USN:L4N3LD139 TEXT:"driver assistance system"] March 2024, with Germany as its sponsor Tesla has called FSD approval key to boosting sales in Europe, where it is seeking to regain market share amid growing competition from Chinese electric-vehicle makers

item.title: Trump says he talked to Xi about the Iran war
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Friday he discussed the Iran war with Chinese President Xi Jinping, as the US ambassador to China said Trump in White House talks made clear that Chinese help for Iran is unacceptable.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Susan Heavey, Katharine Jackson
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Friday he discussed the Iran war with Chinese President Xi Jinping, as the US ambassador to China said Trump in White House talks made clear that Chinese help for Iran is unacceptable. "We did," Trump told reporters when asked whether he talked to Xi about Iran. "I think we're going to do great." The US Ambassador to China David Perdue in a Friday CNBC interview said Trump reiterated to Xi that direct or indirect support for Iran was "totally unacceptable." Asked separately on Fox News if that meant China would stop assisting Iran, Perdue said Washington received assurances from Beijing on Thursday. "We've seen movement ... on that already. That's what the commitment is. They assured us yesterday they're not doing that," Perdue told Fox News' "America's Newsroom" program. Trump and Xi did not take formal questions during the three-day state visit to Washington. Earlier this month, Trump [USN:L8N4550G3 TEXT:"brushed aside"] a report that Iran acquired satellite images of a base in Jordan from Chinese entities before an attack that killed three US troops there in July. "They basically do what we do," Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on September 13. "When they say China spies on us, I say you're right and we spy on them too."

item.title: Dólar cae ante descenso del petróleo, mientras el yen se fortalece
item.description: El dólar caía el viernes por el declive de los precios del crudo, pero se encaminaba a su segunda alza semanal consecutiva por el aumento de las apuestas a una subida de tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.content:encoded: El dólar caía el viernes por el declive de los precios del crudo, pero se encaminaba a su segunda alza semanal consecutiva por el aumento de las apuestas a una subida de tasas de interés. * Por su parte, el yen se apreciaba después de que Japón afirmara que sigue comprometido con Washington con la postura que sustentó la intervención conjunta de julio. * El dólar se encaminaba a romper una racha de cuatro días al alza, en una sesión en la que los precios del crudo restaban más de un 1%, aunque siguen por encima de los 100 dólares el barril, lo que sigue ejerciendo presión al alza sobre la inflación. * "Hemos asistido a un repunte bastante agresivo del dólar en los últimos días y quizá se haya extendido un poco, por lo que ahora se está tomando un pequeño respiro. Así que no diría que se esté debilitando mucho hoy", afirmó Eugene Epstein, de Moneycorp en Stamford, Connecticut. * El índice dólar restaba un 0,34%, a 100,95 unidades, en camino a su mayor declive porcentual diario desde el 3 de septiembre. El euro ganaba un 0,2%, a 1,1402 dólares, pero se encamina a su tercera baja semanal consecutiva. * La libra esterlina mejoraba un 0,24%, a 1,3247 dólares, impulsada por comentarios de línea dura del gobernador del Banco de Inglaterra, Andrew Bailey. No obstante, seguía cerca del mínimo de tres meses alcanzado en la víspera. * El yen repuntaba un 1,09%, en camino de romper una racha de cuatro días de caídas y registrar su mayor alza diaria frente al dólar desde el 7 de septiembre, a 157,13 unidades por dólar. * La moneda nipona subió después de que la ministra de Finanzas de Japón, Satsuki Katayama, afirmara que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, expresó su preocupación por la debilidad del yen durante una cumbre con la primera ministra japonesa, Sanae Takaichi, esta semana.

item.title: Germany's BASF approaches Evonik to create global chemicals giant
item.description: Germany's BASF , among the world's largest chemicals makers, has approached smaller peer Evonik over a possible takeover that could strengthen its portfolio as European companies face tough competition from China.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Inverardi
item.content:encoded: Germany's BASF (BASFn.DE) , among the world's largest chemicals makers, has approached smaller peer Evonik (EVKn.DE) over a possible takeover that could strengthen its portfolio as European companies face tough competition from China. BASF said it continuously evaluated "the strategic option of acquisitions that strengthen its core businesses, deliver a strong strategic fit, drive profitable growth and create value" and was in exploratory talks. Evonik said earlier it had "received a non-binding approach from BASF regarding a voluntary public takeover offer for all shares of the company". RAG Foundation, which holds 43% in Evonik, also said it had been contacted by BASF regarding a takeover offer for Evonik. BASF has a market capitalisation of €45.8 billion ($52.2 billion), while Evonik is currently valued at €9.2 billion. A deal is far from certain. BASF in a statement said the outcome of the exploratory talks was "open at this stage", while Evonik said no discussion was underway. Evonik shares continued a recent rally that traders said was partly driven by takeover speculation. The stock closed 7.2% higher on Friday. BASF shares fell 3.6%.
